unaugmented pluperfect, with neuter plural subject

pluperfect passive of εἰλύω 'wrap, cover'; singular with the neuter plural πάντα
= πάντα; τ → θ before rough breathing
instrumental: the spray, already suggested by ἐρευγόμενον (Merry on 5.403); ἁλὸς ἄχνη as Iliad 4.426

404.n: epic gen. pl. (Attic νεῶν); objective genitive with ὄχοι
masculine ὄχος 'holder, shelter' (ἔχω), in apposition to λιμένες: 'harbors that hold ships'; not the neuter ὄχεα 'chariot'; in Homer only here
not harbors but roadsteads, where ships may lie under the lee of the land (Merry on 5.404); cf. ἰωγή 'shelter' (14.533); in Homer only here

405.n: 'rocks the sea breaks over'; jagged, broken rocks, by the scholia (Merry on 5.405)
'crag, rock' (πήγνυμι), something massive, not necessarily a level reef, as πάγοι ὀξέες 411 (Merry on 5.405); in Homer only here and 411

406.n: epic gen. -ῆος; possessive genitive with γούνατα and ἦτορ
root aorist middle (λύτο), unaugmented, passive in sense; singular with the neuter plural γούνατα; the line = 297, after Iliad 21.114 (and 4.703)

407.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. sg. masc.
407.n: 'be vexed, troubled'; the line = 298, 355, 464 and Iliad 11.403
possessive ὅς (= ἑόν), not the relative

408.n: 'unhoped for' (ἀ- + ἔλπομαι); predicative with γαῖαν; in Homer only here

409.n: 'the depth, gulf' of the sea; object of διατμήξας, as λαῖτμα διέτμαγον 7.276 (Merry on 5.409)

409.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. sg. masc.
409.n: 'cutting through' the water (διά + τμήγω, an epic by-form of τέμνω)
Ionic aorist (= ἐπέρασα) 'crossed'; Merry prints ἐτέλεσσα, 'completed (my course)', with ἐπέρασσα a variant in the scholia (Merry on 5.409 and his critical note)

410.n: 'way out, place to land' (ἐκβαίνω); the apodosis begins here (Merry on 5.410); in Homer only here
accent from enclitic πῃ; οὔ πῃ 'nowhere'

epic gen. -οιο; two-termination, with feminine ἁλός

412.n: perfect with present sense (βέβρυχα), as Iliad 17.264 of a wave at a river mouth
'rushing, dashing' (cf. παλιρρόθιον 430), agreeing with κῦμα; in Homer only here
'smooth, sheer'; λισσὴ δʼ ἀναδέδρομε πέτρη again 10.4, λισσὴ … πέτρη 3.293
perfect with present sense (ἀνα- + δέδρομα, perfect of τρέχω): 'runs up, rises sheer'

413.n: 'deep close to shore' (ἄγχι 'near' + βαθύς 'deep'); two-termination; ἐστί understood; in Homer only here
accented ἔστι 'it is possible', + inf. στήμεναι (414)
epic dat. pl. -εσσι; instrumental, with ἀμφοτέροισι (414)

415.n: accent from enclitic πως; 'lest', of what he fears, as 356 (Merry on 5.415)

415.p: verb · pres. part. act. acc. sg. masc.

415.n: subjunctive after μή; the subject is κῦμα (416)
'stony, rocky' (λίθος), with πέτρῃ; in Homer only here

416.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. sg. neut.

accent from enclitic μʼ; 'lest', with the subjunctive φέρῃ (420)

419.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. sg. fem.
419.n: 'snatch up'; aorist in -ξ-; agrees with θύελλα

epic -σσ-; 'set on, send against', + dat.; subjunctive, still after μή (419)

οἷά τε 'such as'; second accent from enclitic τε
the sea goddess; in Homer only in the Odyssey (also 3.91, 12.60, 12.97)

423.n: perfect of ὀδύσσομαι 'be angry', + dat.; the perfect only here in Homer (aorist ὠδύσατʼ 340)

424.n: epic ἧος = ἕως; the line = 365, 4.120 and Iliad 1.193
elided ταῦτα; τ → θ before rough breathing

425.n: accent from enclitic μιν; δέ in the apodosis
= ἐπί, set between adjective and noun

accusative, like ὀστέα, with the passive verbs: 'he would have been stripped of his skin' (Merry on 5.426)

in tmesis: σὺν … ἀράχθη = συνηράχθη, unaugmented

427.n: ἐπὶ φρεσὶ θῆκε 'put it in his mind', as Iliad 1.55
unaugmented (= ἔθηκε); what she prompted is told by the indicative λάβε (428), not by an infinitive as elsewhere (Merry on 5.427)

428.p: verb · pf. part. mid./pass. nom. sg. masc.
428.n: epic perfect participle ἐπεσσύμενος 'rushing on', with present sense
genitive of the thing grasped; Ionic πέτρη = πέτρα

429.n: unaugmented (= εἴχετο); middle + gen. 'hold on to'

429.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

'surging back' (πάλιν + ῥόθιος, cf. 412): the wave running back; κῦμα understood; again 9.485

431.p: verb · pf. part. mid./pass. nom. sg. neut.
431.n: agrees with παλιρρόθιον, the wave, not with μιν: Odysseus flings himself on the rock (428), the wave on him (Merry on 5.431); Ixion read ἀπεσσύμενον (Merry's critical note)

432.n: ὡς δʼ ὅτε, a simile whose verb is ἔχονται (433)
epic πουλύπους = πολύπους 'many-footed': the octopus; genitive absolute with ἐξελκομένοιο; in Homer only here

'pebble' (cf. λᾶας 'stone'); in Homer only here and 6.95

epic gen. pl. -άων; θρασειάων ἀπὸ χειρῶν as Iliad 11.553 (of darts)

435.n: plural, the skin of the hands

436.n: with the aorist indicative ὤλετο: unreal past
ὑπὲρ μόρον 'beyond (= against) fate', as 1.34–35 (Merry on 5.436)

437.n: 'thoughtfulness, prudence' (Merry on 5.437); the plural at 19.22; a variant reads εἰ μὴ ἐπὶ φρεσὶ θῆκε, as 427 (Merry's critical note)

article used as relative; plural after the collective κύματος (Merry on 5.438)
singular verb with the neuter plural τά: 'belch, spew'
ἤπειρον (ἤπειρος 'land') with the suffix -δε 'to', printed as one word: 'landward', against the shore

Ionic ἐς = εἰς; join ἐς γαῖαν ὁρώμενος (Merry on 5.439)

439.p: verb · pres. part. mid. nom. sg. masc.

optative after a past tense; 439–440 as 417–418

epic gen. -οιο; spelled here with one ρ (also καλλίροον 17.206)

442.n: mixed aorist ἷξον of ἵκω (= ἱκνέομαι), with κατὰ στόμα (441)

epic aorist ἐεισάμην of εἴδομαι 'seem' (not εἶμι 'go')

443.n: with the genitive πετράων: 'smooth of rocks', free from them, as ἄκμηνος σίτοιο Iliad 19.163 (Merry on 5.443); the line again 7.282
epic gen. pl. -άων; genitive of separation with λεῖος
'shelter, cover', + gen. ἀνέμοιο 'from the wind'; in Homer only in the Odyssey
epic gen. -οιο; genitive with σκέπας: 'shelter against the wind'

nominative form in vocative use; the river god

445.p: indef. rel. pron. · nom. sg. masc.

present with perfect sense: 'I am come', + acc.

epic σαόω = σῴζω; with ἐς (453): 'brought safe into'

dual, with the plurals γούνατα and χεῖρας (454)

unaugmented (= ἠγέρθη): his spirit rallied, as Iliad 4.152 (Merry on 5.458); the half-line as Iliad 22.475, again 24.349

epic gen. -οιο; θεός of a goddess (Ino)

462.n: epic dat. pl. -ῃσι(ν); φίλος of one's own limbs: 'her own'

462.n: passive form, middle sense: 'sidling away, withdrawing' (Merry on 5.462)

aorist passive, middle sense: 'lay down under (cover of)'; in Homer only here

possessive ὅς (= ἑόν), not the relative

deliberative subjunctive: 'what will happen to me?'

two-termination in -υς; 'freshening' (θάλλω), here with a suggestion of 'cold' (Merry on 5.467)

subjunctive after μή (467); singular with the two subjects

with μʼ (467): the whole and the part

469.n: 'breeze', Ionic -η; in Homer only here; a scholion reads αὔρη γάρ (Merry's critical note)
ἠῶθι πρό 'early, at first light', πρό adverbial, as Iliad 11.50 (Merry on 5.469)

473.n: epic present 'fear'; the apodosis of εἰ δέ κεν (470)
epic dat. pl. -εσσι(ν); dative of interest: 'prey for beasts'
'what one lights upon' (κυρέω); ἕλωρ καὶ κύρμα as Iliad 5.488

474.n: 'thus', pointing to what he then did (475)

475.n: unaugmented root aorist (= ἔβη); βῆ … ἴμεν 'set off'

476.n: used as a noun: 'in a place seen all round', a clearing with open ground about it (Merry on 5.476)
epic aorist ἤλυθον (= ἦλθον); + acc. 'go under'

ὁμός 'same' + -θεν 'from': 'from the same place', or even 'from one root' (Merry on 5.477); in Homer only here

477.p: verb · pf. part. act. acc. pl. masc.
477.n: epic perfect participle (= πεφυκότας), intransitive: 'grown, growing'

genitive of material; generally taken, with Eustathius, the scholia and Dioscorides, as the wild olive, by some as a thorny evergreen (Merry on 5.477); in Homer only here

root aorist, epic 3 pl. ἔφυν (= ἔφυσαν), intransitive
'alternately, interlacing' (ἀμείβω), their branches crossing; in Homer only here
= ὑπό; in tmesis with δύσετʼ (482): join ὑπὸ-δύσετο (Merry on 5.481)

epic dat. pl. -ῃσι(ν); φίλος of one's own limbs: 'his own'

athematic present of ἔρυμαι 'protect, guard' (not ἐρύω 'draw')

gnomic aorist in the simile: 'hide in', + dat.; in Homer only here

μή in a relative clause of a supposed case

ἄλλος + -θεν 'from': 'from elsewhere', from a neighbor's hearth
